decisive_items: ST segments elevated 4-6 mm in leads II, III and aVF, with ST depression in leads V2-V6
widespread ST-segment elevations (4-15 mm) in leads II, III, aVF, and V2-V6
10% stenosis in proximal left anterior descending artery (LAD) and right coronary artery (RCA)
response.rationale: Transient widespread ST elevations with AV block/VT and non-obstructive coronaries are classic for coronary vasospasm; alcohol is a recognized trigger. Other candidates are either ECG epiphenomena, lack structural evidence, or do not explain the diffuse ST-elevation pattern.

rejected.why: No LV outflow obstruction, septal hypertrophy, or dynamic gradient; ST elevations and non-obstructive coronaries are not explained by HOCM.
AV block is a manifestation of the underlying ischemic/vasospastic episode, not a standalone diagnosis.
Chronic alcohol use is present but no heart failure/cardiomyopathy phenotype; normal troponin and ST elevations favor vasospasm rather than toxic cardiomyopathy.
